_comment: The type glyph for a row: what it IS, before you read it.
Dave, 2026-09-16: 'let's use icons like Jarvis does to identify
categories instead of the color highlight.' Same anatomy JARVIS
approved on 2026-08-18: a bare colored glyph, no tile behind it.
Redrawn 2026-09-17, Dave: 'let's improve the quality of the icons.'
Four things were wrong and none of them was the choice of shape:
1. Stroke. 1.75 on a 24 box drawn at 18px is a 1.31px line, which on
a phone lands between device pixels and reads soft. The renderer
now draws at 2.0 on 20px, a 1.67px line, and the whole set looks
sharper without a single path changing.
2. Safe area. Several glyphs ran to the edge of the box (people out
to x=1 and x=23, warning to y=20.5), so they optically sat larger
than their neighbours and clipped at small sizes. Everything is
now inside a 20x20 area with 2 units of padding.
3. Detail below the resolution. The trophy's handles, the megaphone's
sound arcs and the medal's ribbon carried features under 2 units,
which merge into a blob at 18px. Redrawn with nothing finer.
4. Two glyphs said the wrong thing. `visit` was a calendar, which is
a date and not a campus visit, and is now a pin. `pledge` was the
clock glyph exactly, so a pledge and a deadline were the same
mark; it is now a calendar carrying a money mark, which is what a
pledge is: an amount and a date it is due.
`board` was a bar chart and is now kanban columns, which is the
recruiting board. The board of directors got its own `governance`
glyph, seats around a table, because the two were sharing one mark
and they are not the same thing.
The `stage_*` set is new. Pills lost their colour fill in the same
pass, so the stage a target is at now needs a shape of its own
rather than a coloured background. They are deliberately plain:
a stage mark sits next to a type glyph and must not compete with it.
JSON rather than a .ts file because the prototype and the preview
generators read it too. A copy in each generator drifted three times
in one sitting the last time it was tried, so there is one file and
everything parses it.
Every path is drawn on a 24x24 box, stroked not filled, so one set
works at any size and in either theme. Stroke width, caps and joins
are set by the renderer, never inline.
